PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 0 °C

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Photoelectric effect? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Photoelectric effect.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Photoelectric effect.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Photoelectric effect.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mains electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mains electricity.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mains electricity.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Mains electricity.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mains electricity.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Circular motion? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Circular motion.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Circular motion.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Circular motion.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Circular motion.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Circular motion and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Floating and Sinking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Quantity of Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Thin lenses and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — 100 °C

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.

3. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mains electricity.

6. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.

7. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. D — Ice melting to water

10. C — Producers

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites.

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Circular motion.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Circular motion; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Floating and Sinking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Quantity of Heat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Thin lenses; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
